newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Novus Q2 sales, oil/gas production a record.
newsitem.headline: Novus Q2 sales, oil/gas production a record.

text.p: Novus Petroleum Ltd said on Tuesday its production and net revenue for the second quarter ended June 30, 1997 were a record, despite a fall in oil prices.
Production for the June quarter rose 23 percent on the preceding quarter to 2.39 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe), Novus said.
Net revenue rose 18 percent to a record A$35.3 million from A$29.8 million in the March 1997 quarter, despite a fall in the realised oil price to A$24.26 from A$28.60.
The production rise was due mainly to increased Indonesian oil production and a sharp increase in gas production from Oman.
Elsewhere, Novus said it had not yet been possible to establish the full potential of the Singa field in Sumatra, where the Singa-1 well confirmed significant gas flows earlier this month.
"Singa clearly has the dimensions and production capacity to make it readily commercial, with first gas in possibly as little as 12 to 18 months," Novus managing director Bob Williams said.
"And because the well was difficult to engineer, it was not possible to establish the full potential of the Singa field, leaving a substantial amount of untouched upside."
Novus was up four cents at A$4.84 at 3.55 p.m. (0555 GMT).
